description.en: A dedicated ride for small satellites. Cheap and quick to book, but it only lifts a few hundred kilograms.
description.zh-TW: 小衛星專用的火箭。便宜、排程快，但只載得動幾百公斤。

source.title: Rocket Lab Form 10-Q, quarter ended 2026-06-30 (SEC EDGAR); Wikipedia: Rocket Lab Electron; NASA SST-SoA Table 10-1; Spaceflight Now (CAPSTONE, 2020)
source.note: sourced: average launch revenue US$9.1M per launch in Q2 2026 (Rocket Lab publishes no list price; the often-quoted $7.5M is older), LEO 300 kg (vendor; NASA SoA lists 200), 500 km SSO 200 kg, 95 of 99 launches successful (4 failures: 2017, 2020, 2021, 2023; count as of November 2026), fairing 1.2 m. CAPSTONE 25 kg to the Moon (with Photon kick stage). estimate: 150 kg to 700 km SSO, 9-month lead time

sources.title: NASA Small Satellite blog: Rocket Lab TROPICS timeline of events (2023-05-25)
sources.note: sourced (page says all times approximate): supersonic T+1:00, Max-Q T+1:11, MECO T+2:29, stage separation T+2:33, stage 2 ignition T+2:36, fairing T+3:08, battery hot swap T+6:52, SECO T+9:27, kick stage separation T+9:31, Curie ignition T+31:00, cutoff T+33:40, payload deployed ~T+33:45. estimate: the same profile is used for every orbit

description.en: The workhorse. Enormous capacity for a satellite this size and an excellent record, but a dedicated flight costs about $70M.
description.zh-TW: 主力火箭。對這種大小的衛星來說運力綽綽有餘、紀錄極佳，但包一整枚要價約 7 千萬美元。

source.title: SpaceX Capabilities & Services (2025 snapshot); Wikipedia: List of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches
source.note: All capacities are for the reusable booster that the standard price buys. sourced (SpaceX 2025): standard price $69.85M, reusable LEO 17,400 kg, 5.2 m fairing; the standard price covers payloads up to 5.5 t to GTO (SpaceX price-list threshold; the 8,300 kg GTO figure needs an expended booster and costs more). sourced (Wikipedia list, count as of November 2026): 698 of 701 launches successful. derived: GEO 3,100 kg = 5,500 kg GTO x exp(-1.8 km/s / (320 s x g0)) with the satellite's own kick motor. estimate: SSO 11,000 kg; TLI ~3,300 kg (expendable ~5,000 kg scaled by the 5.5/8.3 GTO ratio) -> lunar orbit 2,500 kg; 18-month lead time. Secondary sources report a 2026 list price near $74M

sources.title: Spaceflight Now: Timeline for Falcon 9 launch of Starlink satellites (2019)
sources.note: sourced: Max-Q T+1:14, MECO T+2:33, stage separation T+2:36, second stage ignition T+2:43

sources.title: Spaceflight Now: Timeline for Falcon 9's launch of the GPS 3 SV03 spacecraft (2020)
sources.note: sourced: fairing jettison T+3:28, SECO-1 T+8:07. estimate: post-SECO profiles per orbit (LEO direct ~T+12 min like Dragon cargo; SSO two-burn ~T+55 min; GTO ~T+32 min; lunar TLI ~T+48 min like IM-1, 2024)

description.en: Three cores strapped together. Only worth it for very heavy payloads or far destinations, and it has flown far fewer times.
description.zh-TW: 三支核心級綁在一起。只有很重的酬載或很遠的目的地才划算，飛行次數也少得多。

source.title: Wikipedia: Falcon Heavy (SpaceX list price, 2022); KeepTrack: Falcon Heavy launch history (2018-2026)
source.note: All capacities are for the recoverable configuration that the $97M list price buys; the famous 63,800 kg LEO / 26,700 kg GTO figures need all three cores expended. sourced: $97M list price (2022) for payloads up to 8 t to GTO (SpaceX price-list threshold); 14 of 14 successful (ViaSat-3 F3, Roman and NROL-97 flew in 2026; count as of November 2026). derived: reliability 0.94 = (14+1)/(14+2) (Laplace rule: few flights = more uncertainty); GEO 4,500 kg = 8,000 kg GTO x exp(-1.8 km/s / (320 s x g0)). estimate: LEO 30,000 kg and SSO 20,000 kg (SpaceX publishes no recoverable figures), TLI ~4,800 kg (expendable ~16 t scaled by the 8/26.7 GTO ratio) -> lunar orbit 3,600 kg, 30-month lead time

sources.title: Spaceflight Now: Launch timeline for Falcon Heavy's second flight (2019)
sources.note: sourced: side booster cutoff T+2:30, booster separation T+2:34. Europa Clipper (2024): Max-Q T+1:07, SECO-1 T+7:53. estimate: center core MECO ~T+3:05, fairing ~T+3:45; post-SECO profiles as Falcon 9

description.en: A solid-fuel launcher used for small NASA science missions. Before 2009 it had six successes in seven flights.
description.zh-TW: NASA 小型科學任務用的固體燃料火箭。2009 年以前七次飛行成功六次。

source.title: OCO launch press kit (NASA/JPL 2009); Spaceflight Now (2010, 2012); OCO Mishap Investigation summary
source.note: sourced: up to 1,350 kg to LEO; 'six successful missions... 86-percent success rate'; launch contract ~$70M; 63-inch (1.6 m) fairing. estimate: ~800 kg to 705 km SSO, 24-month lead time

sources.title: Universe Today: OCO press conference notes (2009); Spaceflight Now / NASA: Glory launch (2011)
sources.note: sourced: four solid stages (Castor 120 stage 0, Orion 50S XL, Orion 50 XL, Orion 38); stage 0 burns about 1 min 24 s and separates 5 s later; Glory's fairing should have separated at T+2:58; Glory planned separation T+13:05 after a 72 s final burn. estimate: Max-Q, intermediate stage burnout and separation times

description.en: The long-serving launcher that finally carried OCO-2 to orbit: 149 successful flights, but about twice the price.
description.zh-TW: 服役多年的火箭，最後把 OCO-2 送上軌道：149 次成功，但價格約為兩倍。

source.title: OCO-2 launch press kit (NASA/JPL 2014); NASA contract release C12-028 (2012)
source.note: sourced: 149 successful launches, 98% success rate; 10-ft (3 m) fairing. derived: ~$137M = $412M / 3 missions (SMAP, OCO-2, JPSS-1). estimate: ~1,500 kg to 705 km SSO for the 7320 (the 6,100 kg quoted in the press kit is the family maximum), 2,800 kg to 400 km

sources.title: ULA: Delta II OCO-2 mission booklet (Delta II 7320-10, 2014)
sources.note: sourced: three 40 in. x 42 ft solid motors; Mach 1 T+35.7 s, Max-Q 49.7 s, SRM burnout 64.0 s, SRM jettison 99.0 s, MECO 264.2 s, first-stage separation 272.2 s, second-stage ignition 277.7 s, fairing jettison 301.0 s, SECO-1 620.5 s, restart 3050.0 s, SECO-2 3062.4 s, OCO-2 separation 3375.0 s (T+56:15)

description.en: A seat on a rocket full of small satellites. Very cheap, but it only goes where the mission is headed: a dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit.
description.zh-TW: 搭一枚載滿小衛星的火箭。非常便宜，但只能去這趟任務的目的地：晨昏太陽同步軌道。

source.title: New Space Economy: SpaceX rideshare pricing as of February 2026; NASASpaceFlight.com: Transporter-18 (October 2026)
source.note: sourced (secondary): Transporter rideshare to SSO, $350,000 for the first 50 kg and $7,000/kg after (2026 list); Transporter-18 flew on 2026-10-01 (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/10/transporter-18/). derived: a 200 kg slot = $1.4M. estimate: the destination is fixed by the mission (dawn-dusk SSO in this game), Falcon 9 reliability and timeline
